items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: Sal Nistico was still on the band... Frank Tiberi, who was with the band... all those guys would share their knowledge.

ctx.x: So Woody Herman was, who was on the band at that time that showed you the ropes, that sort of jazz education that you can’t get in school? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

Yeah — let’s see Alan Broadbent, who had been a classmate, although we didn’t really engage that much at Berklee, but he was there when I was there. He was on the band. He helped me. Sal Nistico was still on the band and Sal was someone that we really admired coming from Western, New York — he was from Syracuse. He was there. Frank Tiberi, who was with the band probably the longest of anybody, he was still there in the sax section and he always had advice for every drummer. So yeah, he was — all those guys would…
What might you have done that Woody Herman would not like, as a drummer?
